blocks.prompt: 8. A particle moving in a straight line starts from rest and is accelerated uniformly to attain a velocity of 30 km/h in 5 seconds. Find the distance travelled by the particle in the last three seconds.
blocks.explanation:
Uniform acceleration from rest, so the equations of motion apply.
Given: \(u = 0\), \(v = 30\) km/h at \(t = 5\) s. Find: the distance from \(t = 2\) s to \(t = 5\) s.
Plan: change to m/s, find \(a\) from \(v = u + at\), then work out \(x(5) - x(2)\).
steps:
Given: \(u = 0\), \(v = 30\) km/h when \(t = 5\) s, acceleration uniform.
To find: the distance travelled in the last three seconds, that is from \(t = 2\) s to \(t = 5\) s.
Method: The acceleration is constant, so \(v = u + at\) gives \(a\), and \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) gives the position at any time. The distance in the last 3 s is \(x(5) - x(2)\).

Change km/h into m/s
\[v = 30 \times \dfrac{1000}{3600}\]
\[v = \dfrac{25}{3}\ \text{m/s}\]
Why: The time is in seconds, so the velocity must be in metres per second: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s (multiply by 5/18).

Find the acceleration
\[\dfrac{25}{3} = 0 + a(5)\]
\[a = \dfrac{25}{15} = \dfrac{5}{3}\ \text{m/s}^2\]
Why: \(v = u + at\) contains the known \(u\), \(v\), \(t\) and the one unknown \(a\).

Position at any time
\[x(t) = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{5}{3}t^2\]
\[x(t) = \dfrac{5}{6}t^2\]
Why: \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) with \(u = 0\), measuring \(x\) from the starting point.

Positions at t = 5 s and t = 2 s
\[x(5) = \dfrac{5}{6}(25) = \dfrac{125}{6}\ \text{m}\]
\[x(2) = \dfrac{5}{6}(4) = \dfrac{20}{6}\ \text{m}\]
Why: The last three seconds of a 5-second motion begin at \(t = 5 - 3 = 2\) s.

Distance in the last three seconds
\[x(5) - x(2) = \dfrac{125 - 20}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{105}{6} = 17.5\ \text{m}\]
Why: The velocity \(v = \frac{5}{3}t\) is never negative, so the particle never turns back and the distance equals the change in position.

Check
\[v(2) = \dfrac{5}{3}(2) = \dfrac{10}{3}\ \text{m/s}\]
\[x = \dfrac{10}{3}(3) + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{5}{3}(3)^2\]
\[= 10 + 7.5 = 17.5\ \text{m}\ \checkmark\]
Why: Treat the last 3 s as a new motion that starts with the velocity at \(t = 2\) s; \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) gives the same distance.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The book prints no answer for Exercise 7.1, so this answer is ours. It was checked independently with a computer algebra system and against an independent worked solution. Common mistake: the first three seconds give only \(x(3) = 7.5\) m; the question asks for the last three.
